children: By Sukanya Mitra and Rajendra Jadhav
Gold demand in India was subdued this week as volatile prices discouraged purchases, while investment demand remained strong in top consumer China.
In India, domestic gold prices (MAUc1) were trading around 150,900 rupees per 10 grams on Friday after rising to 164,773 rupees last month, the highest level in nearly six months.
"Gold prices have seen sharp swings over the past month. With prices now correcting, buyers are holding back, hoping for a deeper dip before stepping in," a Chennai-based bullion dealer said.
Dealers quoted discount (XAU-IN-PREM) of up to $75 an ounce over official domestic prices this week, inclusive of 15% import and 3% sales levies, compared with last week's discount of up to $54.
"Jewellers are growing cautious about demand during the upcoming festival season and are reluctant to build large inventories," a Mumbai-based bullion dealer with a private bank said.
In China, bullion (XAU-CN-PREM) traded at a premium of $8 an ounce to the global benchmark price, compared with premiums of $3.50 to $9 last week.

"Chinese demand remains very much a story of two halves. Jewellery demand has weakened considerably in the face of high and volatile prices, while investment demand for bars and coins remains exceptionally strong. The result is an increasingly investment-led Chinese gold market," said independent analyst Ross Norman.
In Singapore (XAU-SG-PREM), gold was sold between a $1 discount and a $1.70 premium this week, while in Hong Kong (XAU-HK-PREM) it traded at a discount of $0.5 and a $1.70 premium.
Meanwhile, in Japan (XAU-TK-PREM), gold was sold between a $0.25 discount and a $0.5 premium.
The gold market is mixed this week, with both buyers and sellers being active, investment demand has been recovering, a Tokyo-based trader said.
